introduction: “Whoever has an art or handicraft, it is incumbent upon him to endeavor to develop it to the point of perfection.” Most of the readings are short letters of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to particular people, a tailor, a calligrapher, a medical student, an actress, schoolchildren in Beirut, builders of a temple, telling each to become excellent at what they do; around these stand statements that distinction is to be in character and service, not wealth or birth. The Bible honours craft in Bezaleel and in Ben Sira’s artisans who “maintain the state of the world”; Ecclesiastes says to work “with thy might”, Paul “heartily, as to the Lord”, Herbert that sweeping a room so is “fine”. Confucius puts distinction in practice, not nature, and Jeremiah and Paul strip it from wealth and rank as the readings do. Two questions come with the theme. Paul’s runners remind us that only one wins a race, and the servants who must call themselves unprofitable ask what any excellence amounts to.
questions: The readings ask for perfection in a craft “even though that art be as humble as” the humblest. What makes ordinary work worth perfecting, according to these readings and to Herbert?
“I desire distinction for you … but this distinction must not depend upon wealth.” What kinds of distinction do the readings approve, and how do they differ from ambition?
Students are urged to be first in their class. Can everyone be told this? Is the excellence asked for a comparison with others or with one’s own capacity?
Reading 13 advises one craft over many. What is gained and lost by that concentration?
“We are unprofitable servants.” How do the readings hold together striving for excellence and humility about it?

outside.why: The people that ventures furthest into the sea of knowledge excels the rest. Bacon: studies serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability.

Whoever has a craft must bring it to perfection, however humble. The first person in the Bible said to be filled with the spirit of God is a craftsman: Bezaleel, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.
George Herbert on the humblest work: who sweeps a room as for Thy laws, makes that and the action fine.

Joy to the craftsman who perfects his craft and deals equitably. Ben Sira on smiths and potters, who sit in no councils: they will maintain the state of the world, and all their desire is in the work of their craft.
Honour lies in wisdom and character, not in riches and vainglory. Let not the rich man glory in his riches: but let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me.
“I desire distinction for you.” Ye are a chosen generation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you.
Jesus asks for the same kind of distinction: if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others?
Not financial distinction. A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.
Pride in knowledge and refinement, not in ancestors. Confucius: by nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart.
The strong and wealthy are deprived, and a handmaid is mentioned. Not many mighty, not many noble, are called: God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.
Every thing is to attain its paradise, which is its perfection. Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
Many crafts disperse the mind; concentrate on one. This one thing I do: I press toward the mark.
Without method, no perfection. Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
Thoroughness is among the fruits of faith. Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.
Become unique in thy profession. Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.
Be as diligent in your craft as you can. Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
Pursue to the utmost the arts in which you were trained. The master gave to every man according to his several ability, and looked for the increase.
Struggle unceasingly to perfect yourself. Longfellow: to act, that each to-morrow find us farther than to-day.
In affairs one must achieve complete perfection or no fruit is obtained. He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
A man’s work must show what he is. The Dhammapada: fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
Marcus Aurelius: no longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
Cut and sew a garment befitting the people of Bahá: a tailor addressed in the terms of his trade. Paul to Timothy: a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.

The wish to see each one “the foremost professor”, at the head of the class, excelling all other students. Paul uses the race too: they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize. If only one can be first, what is being asked of everyone? Is excellence in these readings a rank or a standard?
Exalt your thoughts, magnify your endeavours. Lives of great men all remind us we can make our lives sublime.
Excel in every branch of knowledge. Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
Be at the head of your class by hard study and true merit. Confucius begins with the pleasure of it: is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
A school that must become evidently the best. As a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation; but let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.
In government, perfect justice and trustworthiness. Render therefore to all their dues: honour to whom honour.
No one is to be respected because his father was a general. Ye shall know them by their fruits.
A mighty edifice to be raised solidly, with refinement and grace. The builders of Jerusalem’s wall every one with one of his hands wrought in the work.
“Shun slothfulness. Be diligent in your work.” Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise.
Work, and wait for the results. Marcus Aurelius, to himself at dawn: I am rising to the work of a human being.
Purity and sanctity are to distinguish the people of Bahá. Whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, if there be any virtue, think on these things.

The excellence of God’s servants is of two kinds. A saying that sets a limit to all of it: when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants. How does one pursue distinction and say this?
Hopkins on where a person’s worth finally lies: this Jack, joke, poor potsherd, is immortal diamond. Is that worth achieved, as the readings’ excellence is, or given?

shortfall: Readings 12 to 23, 27 to 42 and 46 to 49 are brief encouragements to particular students, craftsmen and builders to perfect their work, alike in wording; they share the companions given here rather than each receiving one.

timothy-workman-not-ashamed.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth

sirach-work-of-their-craft.text: they will maintain the state of the world, and all their desire is in the work of their craft
